HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

My father was admitted this month under CGHS benefits for diabetic foot surgery. As very few hospitals in Mumbai are empanelled under Central Government Health Schemes, we were relieved to get admission here.

The OPD procedures went smoothly. We were later informed that the patient would need to be admitted for a short duration (around two days) for surgical treatment. Since a private room was unavailable at the time, we opted for a multi-sharing ward.

Overall, the surgical treatment and interactions with the doctors and specialists were excellent. Dr. Rajeev Singh and his team took great care of the patient and kept us informed about the surgery schedule in advance, ensuring the admission was not done unnecessarily early.

However, the experience with the nursing staff was disappointing. Routine procedures were frequently delayed, and when assistance was requested, the behaviour was often rude towards both patients and visitors. In contrast, the ward-boy staff were more cooperative, welcoming, and helpful.

The discharge process was particularly frustrating. It began around 10:30 AM, but the paperwork was not handled in a timely manner and took over six hours to complete. There was no clear communication, and responsibility for delays was repeatedly shifted between departments. Since both of my parents and many other patients in the ward are diabetic, such prolonged delays are especially challenging. This is not an overreaction, but a genuine concern.

What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

Jayesh Mehta - Age 63 years

I cannot thank the team here enough for the incredible care they provided to my father. From the clean, spacious rooms to the remarkably hospitable staff, we felt well taken care of.

I want to specifically thank RN Tejaswini Patil on the 10th floor. Her kindness and support went above and beyond; she treated my father like her own family.

We also had a great experience with Dr. Bhadresh Dedhia, who was incredibly helpful in keeping my father comfortable and explained every necessary procedure and every diagnosis to us with utmost patience everyday.

To the Management and Staff of Khar PD Hinduja Hospital,

Dr. B.K. Mishra, Dr. Abhijit Wada, and the entire Neurosurgery Team,
